narrative.overview:
This document describes the shipped native AppKit/SwiftUI caption workspace. Its scope is the floating caption panel and conversation outline; it does not establish a new brand identity or restyle settings. “Caption-first native workspace” is an implementation description, not a user-approved creative metaphor.

The workspace uses dark reading surfaces, system type, SF Symbols, and a restrained blue family for translation and outline cues. Captions retain their own reading area; the outline adds topic structure through disclosure and grouped points. Native controls preserve platform interaction and accessibility behavior.
keyCharacteristics: Dark tonal separation between transcript and outline.
Selectable source text with a smaller blue translation beneath it.
Real columns when space permits; native content tabs when compact.
Topic disclosure and grouped updates reduce visible fragmentation.

rules.name: Caption Reading Rule
rules.body: Preserve the transcript as a dedicated reading region; below the split threshold, switch panes rather than compressing two columns.

rules.name: Source Then Translation Rule
rules.body: Place the spoken source first and its translation directly beneath it, regardless of source language.

dos: Do keep the transcript and outline as separate reading regions.
Do use native system type, SF Symbols, segmented selection, and bordered small action buttons.
Do retain selectable captions and outline points, explicit accessibility labels, and keyboard access.
Do preserve manual scrolling and disclosure choices across content updates and width changes.
Do keep prior outline content visible while a grouped update is prepared.
donts: Don't apply this scoped workspace palette as an automatic redesign of settings or other windows.
Don't replace the compact content selector with squeezed side-by-side columns.
Don't treat the toolbar accent and translation blue as one identical source token.
Don't add custom card shadows, decorative text effects, or a new brand metaphor to this workspace without a separate decision.
Don't treat portable HTML/CSS previews as runtime SwiftUI or exact native-control rendering.
